thread:
Nina: quick spot from the int8 bring-up of kestrel-v2q: a tiny but consistent number of funcall parses are failing because keys are coming back in a different order or an optional nested key is missing. low-volume but noisy for short prompts. tagging @Omar @Felix

Nina: example that failed parsing in strict mode:
```
{"meta":{"id":"123"},"action":"create_issue","args":{"title":"payment fail","severity":"P2"}}
# vs sometimes
{"action":"create_issue","args":{"title":"payment fail","severity":"P2"},"meta":{"id":"123"}}
```

Omar: how many? raw numbers please

Nina: canary over 1.5k requests -> strict_parse_fail 0.9% overall. when we enable our soft-retry (up to 2 retries) ~65% of those recover. failures concentrated at batch sizes 1-3 and when tokenizer truncates the tail.

Felix: interesting. sounds like two root causes: serialization nondeterminism + token truncation leading to missing trailing keys. we should avoid assuming key order in legacy handlers, but also need a pragmatic short-term fix.

Sasha: proposal: implement a "canonicalize-and-validate" shim in the toolrouter that will reorder keys into canonical schema order and backfill missing optional keys with null before strict validation. make it opt-in per route and logged. cheaper than pulling the model or disabling int8.

Omar: telemetry question: can we split parse-retries into categories (order-mismatch, missing-key, nonjson) so we know what to target?

Nina: yes. I added a small trace sampler (3%) and dumped payload diffs to s3. sample heatmap shows most are action<->meta swaps and ~20% are small nested-key drops. link: https://redwood-internal/s3/kestrel-canary/1739098765/traces

CanaryBot: Canary summary: kestrel-v2q-int8 run at 2024-03-26T11:22:08Z. requests=1536, strict_parse_fail=0.9%, retries=10, avg_token_latency_ms=38, status=ok

Felix: next steps I suggest: 1) quick opt-in shim in toolrouter (Sasha) 2) add schema-shuffle and token-truncation cases to model onboarding fuzz-suite (Nina) 3) telemetry split for parse-fail reasons (Omar) 4) short PTQ tweak experiment for <32 token prompts (exploratory)

Sasha: I'll sketch the shim. rough design: a small middleware that takes raw model text -> json parse tolerant (allow key order) -> apply schema canonicalizer (reorder keys, insert optional keys as null) -> reserialize normalized json -> pass to existing strict validator. opt-in via route config: {"toolrouter":{"canonicalize_on_parse":true}}. will surface a metric "canonicalizer_invocations" and "canonicalizer_rewrites".

Nina: please also add a sampled diff log when canonicalizer rewrites so we can audit what we changed.

Omar: on thresholds: current hosted canary threshold is 0.2% strict-parse-fail. for canary with shim allowed I propose a 0.35% soft threshold but GA must be <=0.1% on strict routes. open to bikeshedding numbers.

Felix: +1. also add a dashboard pivot by prompt length and batch size; that will show if truncation is the dominant signal.

Nina: I'll put together a PR that: adds the shim prototype, enables the fuzz-suite in CI for new quant models, and wires the parse-failure reason tags into our retry telemetry. planning to run a targeted canary tomorrow with shim toggled.

Sasha: rough impl note: watch out for handlers that rely on stable insertion order for array-of-kv pairs (legacy). shim should be opt-in and we should allow a "preserve_order" flag per route.

Omar: I'll add the telemetry fields and a small alert on "parse_rewrite_rate" > 0.25% for strict routes.

Nina: thanks team. will demo the shim + canary results in the onboarding sync. dropping the small fuzz harness I used: https://redwood-internal/ci/fuzz/schema-fuzzer (includes key-shuffle, optional-drop, tokenizer-edgecases). :rocket
